answer.rationale: Write-path p99 is 5x and called out as confined to the primary region, which is the closest match to the March case where failover restored latency and traffic shifted without dropping work. Release timing is a real competing cause, so rollback stays plausible and is why b1 is being verified alongside b2. Circuit breaking is rejected because failing fast on the write path would risk losing customer writes at settlement peak. Read-replica routing previously helped when report/read load was saturating the primary, which is not the failure mode described here. Capacity remains an alternative if verification weakens the regional story. Uncertainty is preserved: region-scoped write latency could also be an artifact of writes living on the primary plus a bad release or peak overload.
